originality.rationale: The computed claim is the exact same-permutation covariance profile with individual C_j, together with positionwise zeroes for every 3<=j<=n-2. Accessible primary comparisons establish marginal successions, cycle-notation succession laws, Eulerian refinements, or the scalar total-cycle dependence; none of the inspected statements entails the cycle-length vector. In particular knowing the sum over j loses the n-2 zero cancellations. The author-uploaded cycle-successions paper expressly distinguishes joint laws under the correspondence between one-line and cycle notation. Historical-priority uncertainty persists; a negative search is not proof of novelty.
residual_risks: An early or unindexed result might already imply the same-permutation length-resolved covariance, notwithstanding negative current searches.
The full 1979 publisher article was not read, only its accessible abstract.
Some broader permutation-statistics tables may encode the four-mode covariance implicitly; no exhaustive literature census is claimed.

value.rationale: Ordinary successions were introduced and analyzed as a natural shuffling diagnostic; cycle-length counts are a classical invariant of the same permutation. The theorem gives every covariance, with a nontrivial complete zero band for all 3<=j<=n-2 separately at each positional event, and exact plus/minus boundary modes. The previous total-cycle covariance does not recover this distribution of dependence. The finding is a general structural orthogonality result, not a numeric small-case gain; no independent-data or statistical-power claim is made.
